about: One plain sentence or two per later attempt, written only from what the record holds for it (the replicators' own words, a reviewer's note, the paper's title, the recorded size). Every number and name in a line is in its basis. These 16 were written by hand on 2026-10-22 for the four sample pages; the plan is for a cheap model to write the rest from the same inputs and for every line to be read against them.

at_f645dd0967.line: Murtagh and Todd ran two studies of their own and saw no sign of self-regulatory depletion in either.

at_228774d662.line: People in a high-demand condition recalled 54.3% of the words, against 69.8% for people in a low-demand condition. The authors say this replicates Schmeichel’s 2007 finding.

at_34e8ce730c.line: A new group did two tasks that took either high or low effort, then a working-memory test. People who swished a control drink showed no sign of depletion; in the sucrose condition, effort improved performance.

at_549abc29a7.line: People suppressed their emotions during a sad movie clip, then did a Stroop task while their brain responses were recorded. Suppressing emotions weakened error detection afterwards; reappraising them did not.

at_6f38492f05.line: Four new randomized studies, two with community samples and two with young adults, used a letter-crossing task meant to deplete self-control and then tested handgrip or Stroop performance. There was no evidence of depletion in any of the four.

at_899ea22787.line: In one experiment, 70 new participants had a sugar or a non-caloric sweetener drink between two delay-discounting tests, following a 2010 protocol by Wang and Dvorak. A second experiment, with 115 people, tested sensing glucose in the mouth. The authors found no effect of sugar sensing or ingestion on ego depletion.

at_442fef7957.line: A preregistered study of 200 people used the video task from earlier work: a six-minute video watched either while attending to the interviewee and ignoring words on the screen, or with no such rule. A follow-up test came next. People in the depletion condition did not perform worse than the control group.

at_66250baded.line: A preregistered project in 23 labs with 2,141 people tested a sequential-task version of ego depletion; its protocol was based on Sripada et al., not on any exact 1998 task. The effect was small, with a 95% confidence interval that included zero.

at_976f61a082.line: A published two-study replication told some people they had a lucky golf ball and compared their score on a 10-shot golf task with controls. People told they had a lucky ball performed almost identically to controls. The authors write that the failure was not due to lack of impact, lack of statistical power, differences in task difficulty, or differences in participants’ belief in luck.

at_4e2d11f718.line: A Dutch replication study, titled “Does reading literary fiction lead to more empathy?”, reports a non-replication. The authors write that “even when using the exact same selected text samples, methods, and population as Kidd and Castano, one does not necessarily obtain the same results.”

at_475e9ee891.line: This replication tested the original’s Studies 1, 3 and 5. The authors found no significant advantage in scores on the RMET, the photos-of-eyes test, for literary fiction compared to any of the other conditions. A measure of lifetime exposure to fiction, the Author Recognition Test, did consistently predict scores across conditions.

at_abcd332553.line: Four replication experiments asked whether a single session of reading literary fiction improves “mentalising”, the understanding of other people’s thoughts and feelings. In none of the experiments did reading literary fiction have any effect on mentalising relative to control conditions.

at_afb8752ede.line: Part of a project that evaluated the replicability of social-science experiments published in Nature and Science between 2010 and 2015. Its test of the original’s Study 1 had 714 people and is recorded as not replicating.

at_d743a4ae2f.line: The original authors ran three preregistered replications and extensions of their own study. Judged with the “small telescopes” method, two were uninformative failures to replicate and one was a successful replication.

at_f0660a314a.line: A replication tested the effect of reading a short passage of literary fiction on theory of mind. The authors say its results were largely consistent with Kidd and Castano’s original findings.

at_70df8aaff0.line: A conceptual replication used photographs of medalists from the 2000–2016 Olympics and automated coding of their facial expressions. It supported the bronze-versus-silver expression pattern, and it also supported an expectation-based explanation.
